implementation_qualification: Passed native predecessor checks and 11 cached-pilot tests; predictive qualification awaits complete outcome audit.
before_extension: Close the existing one-hour pilot before launching a new scientific experiment or scheduling study. Do not automatically extend the sample or resume the stopped 304-block run.

Verify frozen inputs and full output coverage, all 126 unique record/regime outcomes, forecast sealing before futures, 18 inherited rewrites plus fresh terminal recipient, native flat audits and independent weighted block inference.

Report absolute Brier scores for all three models in both noise regimes, every predeclared paired contrast and interval, calibration, class diagnostics, history counts and cost accounting. No favorable subgroup or noise-regime selection.
Audit weighted calibration and metadata diagnostics at closeout as well as primary contrasts. Additional presentation and arithmetic checks must preserve the frozen estimand and decision rules.
Label incomplete execution, inconclusive precision, predictive support/rejection on the selected panel, and RDT-specific evidence separately. Preserve all prior failures.
scientific_claim: A useful fixed successor forecast can be explained by conventional predictors and error-correction mechanisms. A Brier advantage alone does not identify an RDT-specific mechanism. Any stronger claim needs a separately frozen discriminating prediction against those explanations.

scheduling_target.formula: Delta(z,a) = E[Y_H(repair action a) - Y_H(no repair) | z]
scheduling_target.endpoint: The same declared task, retained distinction, horizon and disturbance distribution on both branches; declare the actual repair intervention and its resource cost.
scheduling_target.pairing: Start paired branches from the same boundary state and use a predeclared coupling of future injuries and noise with correct marginals. Each branch propagates its own state. Include both rescues and harms.
scheduling_target.identity: For binary success, Delta = P(Y_repair=1,Y_control=0) - P(Y_repair=0,Y_control=1). High failure risk alone does not identify either term.
scheduling_target.budget: For a single decision and equal action costs, compare expected benefit rankings. With varying costs, specify a budget-constrained policy and charge measurement, intervention and execution costs. Benefit-per-cost is not automatically an optimal multi-step policy.
scheduling_target.comparisons: At the same total resource budget, retain failure-risk scheduling, direct-probe and ordinary predictors, fixed/periodic or random allocation, and no repair as appropriate controls.
scheduling_target.evidence_boundary: The current continuation pilot has one natural future per record/regime, with no paired repaired/no-repair long-horizon branch. Its risk predictions and retained-versus-rewritten short probes cannot by themselves qualify a repair scheduler.
